note: Starting picks for a scorecard by kind of business. These are suggestions the member changes, not facts: the member picks the numbers and sets every target. No industry benchmarks are used anywhere in the pack.

why.sales: What customers paid. The first number to look at each morning.
why.orders: How many sales. Tells you whether more people bought, or the same people bought more.
why.aov: What one order is worth on average. Bundles and add-ons move it.
why.refunds: Money given back. A jump points at one product or one promise.
why.refund_rate: Refunds as a share of sales, so a busy week and a slow week compare fairly.
why.chargebacks: Payments a customer's bank pulled back. Each one costs a fee and needs an answer fast.
why.fees: What payment companies kept. Worth a look if you take a lot of small payments.
why.cash_in: Sales after fees, refunds and chargebacks: what actually reached your account.
why.ad_spend: What your ads cost. Read it beside what they brought in, never alone.
why.ad_results: Purchases, sign-ups or messages your ads platform counted.
why.cost_per_result: What one result from your ads cost. Compare it with what a customer is worth to you.
why.click_rate: Share of people who saw an ad and clicked. A low one usually means the first line or picture.
why.ad_return: Sales your ad platform counted for each $1 of ad spend. Platforms count generously, so watch the trend.
why.posts: How often you posted. The one marketing number fully in your control.
why.post_views: How many times people saw your posts.
why.engagement: Likes, comments, shares and saves for every 100 views: whether the people who saw it cared.
why.follows: New follows your posts brought in.
why.custom: A number from your own sheet.
